result.text: The bolted stone at Vell Foot is still in place. The survey register describes a brass bolt set into a granite boulder as the fixed point for measurements. It records the instruction, “Do not move the boulder,” then marks it as a joke. The register’s later pencil addition says, “He did measure it, every September.” The survey hut at Vell Foot also remains standing, with its door shut and a kettle on the shelf. Someone pinned a note to the door: “Went up to look at the stakes. Could not find them. Left the tea.” Nobody signed it. I have left the note where it is. An archive can be a place.
